boundary_rationale: This unit opens at the universal summons קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, byte tier), “Come near, you nations, to hear! Listen, you peoples. Let the earth and all it contains hear, the world, and everything that comes from it.” (web:Isa.34.1), an addressee shift from the second-singular “you” of web:Isa.33.1-Isa.33.24 to the nations, peoples, and earth; that imperative pair stands verse-initial at exactly 3 verses book-wide. A second imperative pair opens verse-initially inside the span at דִּרְשׁ֨וּ מֵֽעַל סֵ֤פֶר יְהוָה֙ וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ (oshb:Isa.34.16, byte tier), “Search in the book of Yahweh, and read” (web:Isa.34.16), standing verse-initial at exactly 2 verses book-wide; it names no addressee by vocative, unlike the onset at Isa.34.1, so it does not open a fresh unit of its own. No hoy, massa, or comparable addressee-vocative onset interrupts through web:Isa.34.17 on that ground, and the following chapter opens instead with third-person description at web:Isa.35.1, marking the close. The verse at this unit's own close, oshb:Isa.34.17, carries a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness) that corroborates the break.

device_notes: This oracle's desolation forms a pairing with the following chapter's blossoming description; this row registers that pairing as literary texture rather than as evidence for its own boundary, which rests on web:Isa.34.1's own vocative onset and the register change at web:Isa.35.1. Chapter 34 runs 17 verses in full, and this row claims all of them; confidence sits at medium_low both for that whole-chapter extent and because a second, formally weaker imperative onset stands inside the span at Isa.34.16 -- a genuine interior signal that the row now names rather than passes over in silence, and the band reflects that exposure rather than a defect newly found in the boundary itself.

boundary_rationale: This unit opens at web:Isa.35.1, “The wilderness and the dry land will be glad. The desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.”, a register shift from the preceding chapter's summons-and-desolation to third-person description of flourishing. Two internal imperative addresses open within it: חַזְּק֖וּ יָדַ֣יִם רָפ֑וֹת (oshb:Isa.35.3, byte tier), “Strengthen the weak hands, and make the feeble knees firm.” (web:Isa.35.3); and אִמְרוּ֙ לְנִמְהֲרֵי (oshb:Isa.35.4, byte tier), “Tell those who have a fearful heart” (web:Isa.35.4) -- neither carries the nations-summons vocative that opens web:Isa.34.1, and neither is rested on the presentative הִנֵּ֤ה later in the same verse, a different lexeme standing mid-verse rather than verse-initial. The unit runs to web:Isa.35.10, “Then Yahweh’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”, the frame's own close; the following verse begins the narrative-zone frame and this row does not cross that seam. This same close, oshb:Isa.35.10, carries a parashah PE mark (single-witness); ahead of this unit's own onset, oshb:Isa.34.17 is closed by a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at Isa.35.5 was weighed and declined. The adverb אָ֥ז opens oshb:Isa.35.5, and its form אָ֣ז opens oshb:Isa.35.6 as well (byte tier), two adjacent verse-initial sites out of exactly 6 book-wide; it introduces the healing catalogue but brings no addressee or frame shift of its own, and the descriptive register begun at web:Isa.35.1 carries through both verses into what follows.

device_notes: This blossoming oracle answers the preceding chapter's desolation as the pairing's other half; this row registers that pairing as literary texture, with its own boundary argued from the register shift at web:Isa.35.1 and its own closing formula at web:Isa.35.10 rather than from the pairing itself. A parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness), interior to this unit, falls at oshb:Isa.35.2 at an internal turn, disclosed without driving a cut.
